audit_kind: Read-only APK inspection and updater source/test review; no installation or runtime test

scope.gate_effect: None: G5 conditional and G3/G4 pending remain unchanged. Historical FAIL evidence is not superseded.

tools.note: Build-tools version 36.0.0 does not mean an API36 platform or runtime is installed. apksigner reads public APK certificates only.

packaged_manifest.label: Sumo Controller · Test
packaged_manifest.debug_only_surface_note: Packaged manifest includes exported androidx.compose.ui.tooling.PreviewActivity and androidx.activity.ComponentActivity. This is a debuggable test artifact, not a production-hardened release.

public_signing_identity.classification: Android Debug certificate; not evidence of a project-owned stable distribution key or backup. No private key was opened.

native_abi_inventory.source: Actual APK entries from installed JBR jar tf, corroborated by installed aapt badging; ELF metadata and per-entry SHA256 read directly from this ZIP using Python stdlib.
native_abi_inventory.interpretation: ARM native payload presence is directly observed, NOT inferred from x86_64 AVD execution. Presence of ARM libraries does not establish phone startup, API36 behavior, 16 KB page compatibility, or physical-device functionality.

cache_binding.limit: This binds the current build-output/cache APK to the audited file, not to a phone, installed AVD app, or every current source file. No rebuild occurred.

api36_availability.status: API36 runtime testing unavailable from the inspected installed SDK. No SDK/AVD change made. Remote package availability was not queried and is not claimed.
api36_availability.declared_support_only: minSdk36 permits Android API36 at the manifest level; no API36 execution was performed. targetSdk37 is not a minimum-OS requirement.

updater_review.observed: Both feed and APK URLs must use exact lowercase https, have a host, no userinfo or fragment. Standard platform HTTPS trust is used (no custom trust bypass in this flow). Redirect following is manual; at most 4 requests / 3 redirects, HTTPS and same original host enforced. Only HTTP200 body accepted. Connect/read timeouts are 10/30 seconds; cancellation checked and connections disconnected. Same-host comparison is host-only, not same-origin: ports are not required to match.

Feed limited to 65536 bytes. JSONObject parser requires strings for string fields and integer-form Number values for numeric fields, with Int bounds where applicable. Required fields: schemaVersion,applicationId,versionCode,versionName,minSdk,apkUrl,sizeBytes,sha256,releaseNotes,channel. Only schemaVersion1/channel test supported. versionName nonblank <=100 chars; releaseNotes <=10000 chars; APK 1..100 MiB; SHA256 exactly64 lowercase hex. APK host must match checked feed host. Unknown fields are not rejected; metadata has no independent signed-document validation. APK authenticity remains bound to the installed signer, not merely a metadata hash.

PackageManager supplies actual installed package, longVersionCode, current SDK and signer hashes. Candidate versionCode must be strictly greater than installed and positive; metadata minSdk must be 1..device SDK. APK archive package/versionCode/minSdk must exactly equal metadata, and archive versionName must match metadata.

Download streamed into private cache sumo-update.apk with byte limit; exact actual length and SHA256 required. PackageManager parses APK with GET_SIGNING_CERTIFICATES; archive and installed nonempty signer SHA256 sets must exactly match. Archive is verified after download and again immediately before session creation. Android PackageInstaller performs its own package/signature checks. This audit separately verified the actual packaged APK cryptographically using SDK apksigner. Exact current signer equality does not implement signing-lineage/key-rotation migration.

Download/install reject a feed different from the feed checked for current metadata. State is in memory; a process restart requires check/download again. Cancellation flag is checked in transfer and before installer commit. execute catches errors, deletes cache APK, and clears busy/ready.

MainActivity opens updater only after stopControl gate. Install requires Android canRequestPackageInstalls or opens per-app unknown-sources settings; requestInstall rechecks permission and file. MODE_FULL_INSTALL session specifies package/size, USER_ACTION_REQUIRED and downloaded-file source; bytes are written+fsync then committed to explicit nonexported receiver via mutable broadcast PendingIntent. Session abandoned on synchronous exception. Pending Android confirmation intent is launched by Activity. No silent update, uninstall, key migration or settings clear exists in this path.

Receiver stores only the last message in SharedPreferences sumo_install_result and updates Compose state. Pending confirmation Intent is in memory only. Startup reloads last message; success text explicitly asks user to reopen and verify actual version. Abort/failure do not claim success. No durable session ID, candidate version/hash, timestamp or multi-entry installation ledger is stored. A historic fixture error/status is not evidence that a hosted update succeeded.

reviewed_test_coverage.execution: Source review only; none of these tests was run by this audit. Existing results are not relabeled as fresh passes.

coverage: wrong archive package/version/minSdk/signers, empty signers and size/hash mismatch rejected

tests.limits: Connection is injected fake HttpURLConnection; not real HTTPS/TLS/hosting coverage.

coverage: changed feed rejected before touching installer
JSON string version rejected and malformed JSON fails
current installed APK cannot be passed as metadata version2
abort/storage failures do not claim success
failure message restored across Activity recreation
tests.limits: The process-state test clears static state and recreates Activity; it is not an actual process-kill/reboot test.

coverage: original APK signer set matches installed
mutated classes.dex APK must fail PackageManager signer parsing
tests.limits: Runtime/platform behavior not executed in this audit, especially not API36/ARM.

coverage: optional externally prepared v2 fixture requests actual Android confirmation
installed version remains1 and UI PWM0/0
tests.limits: Assumes candidate instrumentation argument; otherwise skips. Direct local requestInstall bypasses HTTPS; deliberately cancels, so this is not a successful upgrade or A-to-B-to-C test.

unproven: real HTTPS metadata/APK fetch with production TLS/redirect behavior
settings/safety state preservation after successful upgrade on phone
unknown-source permission flow on target OEM
installer confirmation recovery after real process death

installation_and_distribution_limits.assessment: [INFERENCE] Manifest allows API36+ devices with a supported ABI; actual APK includes ARM and x86 variants. No fresh phone install was attempted. Android source-install approval/OEM policy, storage, compatibility, TLS reachability and actual device details remain prerequisites. API<36 is excluded. Existing OS backup/restore can make a nominal fresh install restore prior data because allowBackup=true; no blank-data guarantee.

[INFERENCE] In-place update requires the same package and compatible signing identity; this app further requires strictly increasing versionCode and exactly equal signer sets. The updater does not clear app data, but successful overwrite/data preservation has not been demonstrated. Uninstall/clear-data to bypass a signature conflict can destroy settings, calibration, saved feed, kill state, diagnostics and installer message. Do not use uninstall as an upgrade workaround. Default backup XML is not a verified recovery plan.

This APK is versionCode1. A device already on1 or higher cannot receive this same artifact through the in-app updater (strict > check). It can only be a first-install/baseline candidate or an external installation, not evidence of an in-app upgrade. Rebuilding different bits while keeping versionCode1 does not solve this. External same-version reinstall behavior was not exercised.

Actual artifact is debuggable and Android Debug-signed. Build config has opt-in sumoDistribution stableTest signing and requires version>=2 plus external owner-provided key configuration, but those keys/variables/backup were not accessed or verified. It still configures the debug build signing; stable signing alone would not make it a production release. A differently signed stable candidate cannot overwrite this debug install through the current updater, even with a higher version. No signing-lineage migration exists here. Start any authorized stable phone test chain with a stable-signed baseline; do not promise migration or preserve-data uninstall.

Public certificate proves who signed these bytes, not private-key ownership, key availability, long-term custody or backup. A future build must maintain the intended signer identity; neither an Android Debug subject name nor a build task proves a stable chain. No key material or secret environment configuration was opened.

updater_blockers.item: No validated stable-signed baseline and two strictly newer same-signer update artifacts were supplied or inspected. Current debug v1 cannot demonstrate A->B->C.

Project records report no configured hosting/feed. No authorized real HTTPS feed/APK pair was supplied or fetched in this audit; .invalid/example fixture URLs and last installer message are not hosting evidence.
Inspected SDK has neither API36 platform nor API36 image/sdkmanager. No API36 environment was installed or changed.
No phone or stable-key custody/backup was inspected. ABI payload presence and an x86_64 AVD do not prove ARM/API36 installation, permission UX, successful upgrades or preserved data.

Last-message-only installer history cannot attribute an old success/failure to a particular version/hash/session; pending confirmation is not durable across process loss. Treat actual installed version and a recorded upgrade transaction as acceptance evidence, not a stale message.

conclusion: Packaged identity, hash, public signature, native ABI payloads and cache hash are directly inspected. Updater has explicit HTTPS/metadata/size/hash/package/version/minSdk/signer/install-consent checks with source tests, but phone readiness and successful stable HTTPS upgrades remain unverified and blocked by the listed prerequisites. This audit does not close existing STOP/cadence FAIL history or authorize physical hardware/release.
